name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with a +19 partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Quigley running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger Tommy Hanson has shown no fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Quigley near 95% to win
model.rationale: Quigley holds a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat, has over $1.1 million on hand, and faces an underfunded challenger with no visible support, while markets price him around 95%. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win, keeping this Safe D.
model.watch: A surprise wave-level Republican environment or a serious, well-funded challenger emerging could narrow the margin, though a seat this blue is very unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Chicago-area district that leans about 19 points Democratic. He has raised over $700,000 and holds more than $1.1 million in cash, while Republican Tommy Hanson has reported no fundraising and no outside spending is active in the race. Prediction markets put Quigley's chances near 95 percent.

No public polls cover the general election, so the forecast rests on the district's strong Democratic lean, Quigley's incumbency and financial edge, and the challenger's lack of visible resources. Everything points to a comfortable Quigley victory, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
